1. (Currently Amended) A lavatory unit for an aircraft cabin,wherein the lavatory unit is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration, in which the PRM-accessible configuration of the lavatory unit accommodates (i) a PRM in a wheelchair and allows for a transfer from the wheelchair to the toilet, and (ii) an assistant when one is required by a PRM,
wherein in the able-bodied configuration the lavatory unit has a first internal floor space and there is a cabin floor space external to the lavatory unit,
wherein the lavatory unit is expandable into the PRM-accessible configuration in which the lavatory unit is expanded to have a second internal floor space, the second internal floor space encompassing a region of the cabin floor space.
2. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 1, the lavatory unit comprising a perimeter wall that separates an internal space of the unit from space external to the unit,wherein the perimeter wall comprises a moveable wall assembly;
wherein in the able-bodied configuration the moveable wall assembly is in a retracted configuration,
wherein the moveable wall assembly is moveable into an expanded configuration to expand the lavatory unit into the PRM-accessible configuration.
3. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 2, wherein the lavatory unit comprises at least one panel assembly configured to cover a gap that would
otherwise be created in the perimeter wall of the lavatory unit when the lavatory unit is expanded.
4. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 3, wherein the at least one panel assembly comprises a foldable panel that expands by unfolding.
5. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 3, wherein the at least one panel assembly comprises a sliding panel mounted for movement relative to the moveable wall assembly, and wherein the panel slides from a first position when the lavatory unit is in the able-bodied configuration to a second position when the lavatory unit is in the PRM-accessible configuration and thereby covers a gap that would otherwise be created in the perimeter wall of the lavatory unit as the moveable wall assembly moves between the retracted configuration and the expanded configuration.
6. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 2, wherein the lavatory unit comprises a door assembly,wherein in the able-bodied configuration the door assembly is operable to an open position in which an able-bodied user can access the first internal floor space via a first door opening in the perimeter wall, the first door opening having a first effective width;
wherein in the PRM-accessible configuration the door assembly is operable to an open position in which a PRM can access the internal floor space via a second door opening in the perimeter wall, the second door opening having a second effective width;
and
wherein the second effective width is greater than the first effective width.
7. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 6, wherein the moveable wall assembly comprises the door assembly.
8. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 7, wherein the door assembly comprises a primary door and a secondary door,wherein the primary door provides access to the first door opening; and
the primary door and the secondary door cooperate to provide access to the second door opening.
9. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 1, the lavatory unit comprising a crew seat mounted on an inboard side of the unit.
10. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 1, the lavatory unit comprising a toilet, andwherein in the PRM-accessible configuration, the interior space comprises a recess sized and shaped to receive the knees of a PRM sitting on the toilet and/or a PRM sitting in a wheelchair received within the lavatory unit.
11. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 1, the lavatory unit comprising a sink located adjacent an inboard and/or forward side of the unit.
12. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 1, wherein the maximum length of the lavatory unit in the able-bodied configuration is no more than 38 inches.
13. (Previously Presented) An aircraft comprising a lavatory unit according to claim 1.
14. (Previously Presented) The aircraft according to claim 13, the aircraft cabin comprising a row of seats, an aircraft door, and an egress pathway associated with the aircraft door;wherein the lavatory unit is located aft of the row of seats and immediately adjacent to the egress pathway.
15. (Currently Amended) A method of reconfiguring an aircraft lavatory unit to enable access by a PRM, the method comprising expanding the lavatory unit from an able-bodied configuration to a PRM-accessible configuration in which the lavatory unit accommodates (i) a PRM in a wheelchair and allows for a transfer from the wheelchair to the toilet, and
(ii) an assistant when one is required by a PRM, such that cabin floor space that was located outside the lavatory unit prior to the expansion is encompassed within the internal floor space of the lavatory unit after expansion.
16. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 15, wherein the lavatory unit comprises a moveable wall assembly and expanding the lavatory unit comprises displacing the moveable wall assembly.
17. (Cancelled).
18. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 3, wherein the moveable wall assembly comprises said at least one panel assembly, and said at least one panel assembly is configured to cover a gap that would otherwise be created in the perimeter wall of the lavatory unit when the moveable wall assembly moves from the retracted configuration to the expanded configuration.
19. (Previously Presented) The lavatory unit according to claim 6, wherein in the able- bodied configuration the door assembly is operable to a closed position in which the door assembly prevents access to the first internal floor space via said first door opening;
and wherein in the PRM-accessible configuration the door assembly is operable to a closed position in which the door assembly prevents access to the internal floor space via said second door opening.
20. (Currently Amended) The method according to claim 16, wherein expanding the lavatory unit comprises displacing the moveable wall assembly rearwards relative to the aircraft.
